message.content:
The answer to “what is the best movie of 2020?” depends on how you define “best.”  Critics, audiences, box‑office performance, and award bodies all have different metrics.  Below is a quick snapshot of the most celebrated films of 2020 across a few of those lenses—so you can decide which one fits your definition of “best.”

| Category | Film | Why it stood out |
|----------|------|------------------|
| **Critics’ consensus (Rotten Tomatoes / Metacritic)** | **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** | 97 % on Rotten Tomatoes, 88 /100 on Metacritic.  Praised for its sharp dialogue, strong ensemble cast, and timely political relevance. |
| | **“Soul”** | 98 % on Rotten Tomatoes, 95 /100 on Metacritic.  Won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and was lauded for its originality and emotional depth. |
| | **“The Father”** | 96 % on Rotten Tomatoes, 90 /100 on Metacritic.  Anthony Hopkins’ performance earned him an Oscar for Best Actor. |
| | **“Minari”** | 96 % on Rotten Tomatoes, 84 /100 on Metacritic.  A quiet, heartfelt immigrant story that resonated with critics and audiences alike. |
| | **“Nomadland”** | 94 % on Rotten Tomatoes, 88 /100 on Metacritic.  Won the Oscar for Best Picture and Best Director (Chloé Zhao). |
| **Audience / Box‑office (domestic)** | **“Tenet”** | 1.3 billion USD worldwide (though theatrical release was heavily impacted by COVID‑19).  Known for its ambitious action and mind‑bending narrative. |
| | **“The Invisible Man”** | 1.1 billion USD worldwide.  A modern take on the classic horror story that performed well at the box office. |
| | **“Wonder Woman 1984”** | 1.0 billion USD worldwide.  A superhero film that drew large crowds despite pandemic restrictions. |
| **Awards (Academy Awards)** | **“Nomadland”** | Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actress (Frances McDormand).  The film’s win was historic for its focus on a largely under‑represented community. |
| | **“Soul”** | Best Animated Feature, Best Original Score.  It also received a nomination for Best Picture, a first for an animated film. |
| | **“The Father”** | Best Actor (Anthony Hopkins).  The film’s nomination for Best Picture was a notable achievement for a drama about dementia. |

### How to pick the “best”

| Criterion | What to look for |
|-----------|-----------------|
| **Critical acclaim** | Rotten Tomatoes / Metacritic scores, reviews from major publications. |
| **Audience enjoyment** | IMDb rating, audience scores on Rotten Tomatoes, box‑office receipts. |
| **Award recognition** | Oscars, Golden Globes, BAFTAs, Cannes, etc. |
| **Personal preference** | Genre, themes, performances that resonate with you. |

### Bottom line

If you’re looking for the film that critics universally praised, *The Trial of the Chicago 7* and *Soul* are top contenders.  If you want the film that won the most prestigious awards, *Nomadland* and *Soul* are the clear winners.  For sheer box‑office impact, *Tenet* and *The Invisible Man* dominated the 2020 theatrical landscape.

Feel free to let me know which angle matters most to you, and I can narrow down the recommendation further!
